units.locator: Deterioration of the Demographic Situation in Most Constituent Entities of the Russian Federation
units.text: Deterioration of the Demographic Situation in Most Constituent Entities of the Russian Federation
units.label: Deterioration of the Demographic Situation in Most Constituent Entities of the Russian Federation

units.locator: Deterioration of the Demographic Situation in Most Constituent Entities of the Russian Federation
units.text: Declining birth rates and natural population decrease have been recorded in the Russian Federation since 2016. In 2023, natural population decrease was 0.5 million and the total fertility rate was 1.41 births per woman. From 2010 to 2021, the number of women of active reproductive age, from 20 to 29, fell by 39.9 percent. The number of women of reproductive age is projected to continue declining until 2046. Under the medium variant of the demographic forecast of the Federal State Statistics Service, by the beginning of 2030 the country’s population will decrease by 2.9 million compared with the beginning of 2024.
units.label: Deterioration of the Demographic Situation in Most Constituent Entities of the Russian Federation · “Declining birth rates and natural population decrease have been…”

units.locator: Deterioration of the Demographic Situation in Most Constituent Entities of the Russian Federation
units.text: The number of constituent entities of the Russian Federation experiencing natural population decrease is growing: it reached 70 in 2023, compared with 46 regions in 2016. The greatest natural population decrease is observed in the Central, Volga and Northwestern Federal Districts. The greatest natural increase is observed in the North Caucasian Federal District.
units.label: Deterioration of the Demographic Situation in Most Constituent Entities of the Russian Federation · “The number of constituent entities of the Russian Federation…”

units.locator: Deterioration of the Demographic Situation in Most Constituent Entities of the Russian Federation
units.text: The number of constituent entities of the Russian Federation with negative net migration is increasing, from 50 in 2011–2016 to 54 in 2017–2022. The greatest relative outflow is observed in the Far Eastern and Siberian Federal Districts and in regions of the European North, namely Murmansk and Arkhangelsk Oblasts and the Komi Republic. At the same time, implementation of state policy measures aimed at ensuring economic growth and improving the population’s quality of life in those territories has slowed the rate of population decline.

units.locator: Declining Inflow of Labor Resources into the Russian Federation Due to Increasing Competition in Global Markets
units.text: Declining Inflow of Labor Resources into the Russian Federation Due to Increasing Competition in Global Markets
units.label: Declining Inflow of Labor Resources into the Russian Federation Due to Increasing Competition in Global Markets

units.locator: Declining Inflow of Labor Resources into the Russian Federation Due to Increasing Competition in Global Markets
units.text: Global migration flows have grown steadily in recent decades: the number of migrants rose from 175 million in 2000 to 280 million by 2020. The largest increases occurred in Europe and Asia, from 56.9 million and 49.1 million in 2000 to 86.7 million and 85.6 million in 2020, respectively.
units.label: Declining Inflow of Labor Resources into the Russian Federation Due to Increasing Competition in Global Markets · “Global migration flows have grown steadily in recent decades:…”

units.locator: Declining Inflow of Labor Resources into the Russian Federation Due to Increasing Competition in Global Markets
units.text: The Russian Federation ranks 4th in the world by total number of migrants, at 11.6 million, behind only the United States of America, the Federal Republic of Germany and the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. Over the past 20 years, the main sources of migration to the Russian Federation have been countries of the former Union of Soviet Socialist Republics, including the Republic of Uzbekistan, the Republic of Tajikistan, the Kyrgyz Republic, Ukraine, the Republic of Kazakhstan, the Republic of Belarus and the Republic of Azerbaijan.
units.label: Declining Inflow of Labor Resources into the Russian Federation Due to Increasing Competition in Global Markets · “The Russian Federation ranks 4th in the world by total number…”

units.locator: Declining Inflow of Labor Resources into the Russian Federation Due to Increasing Competition in Global Markets
units.text: Amid declining birth rates and population aging in the most economically developed countries, global competition for labor, including highly qualified personnel, is increasing.
units.label: Declining Inflow of Labor Resources into the Russian Federation Due to Increasing Competition in Global Markets · “Amid declining birth rates and population aging in the most…”

units.locator: Declining Inflow of Labor Resources into the Russian Federation Due to Increasing Competition in Global Markets
units.text: Under these conditions, external migration to the Russian Federation is declining: in 2016 the net migration rate, reflecting the difference between arrivals and departures, was 27.1 per 10000 people, compared with 13.9 per 10000 people in 2023.
units.label: Declining Inflow of Labor Resources into the Russian Federation Due to Increasing Competition in Global Markets · “Under these conditions, external migration to the Russian…”

units.locator: Declining Inflow of Labor Resources into the Russian Federation Due to Increasing Competition in Global Markets
units.text: During the first half of 2024, 4.7 million foreign citizens registered with the migration authorities, one third fewer than in the same period of 2017, when the figure was 7 million. As of 1 July 2024, 2.9 million foreign citizens were on the migration register in the Russian Federation, including 952.6 thousand citizens of the Republic of Uzbekistan (32.9 percent), 667.2 thousand citizens of the Republic of Tajikistan (22.8 percent), and 334 thousand citizens of the Kyrgyz Republic (11.4 percent). Almost half of foreign citizens were registered in the Moscow (42.3 percent) and Saint Petersburg (6.7 percent) urban agglomerations.
units.label: Declining Inflow of Labor Resources into the Russian Federation Due to Increasing Competition in Global Markets · “During the first half of 2024, 4.7 million foreign citizens…”

units.locator: Growing Risks of Labor Shortages
units.text: Growing Risks of Labor Shortages
units.label: Growing Risks of Labor Shortages

units.locator: Growing Risks of Labor Shortages
units.text: The generally unfavorable demographic situation is increasing the risk of labor shortages, primarily in territories with low labor productivity and substantial population outflows. According to the demographic forecast of the Federal State Statistics Service, the country’s working-age population will reach 87.3 million by 2030, after which it will stop growing. With a working-age population of that size, the labor shortage will exceed 2 million.
units.label: Growing Risks of Labor Shortages · “The generally unfavorable demographic situation is increasing…”

units.locator: Growing Risks of Labor Shortages
units.text: Against the backdrop of labor shortages, unemployment measured using the methodology of the International Labour Organization has shown a sustained downward trend, falling in particular from 5.5 percent in 2016 to 3.2 percent in 2023. Relatively high unemployment persists only in the North Caucasian Federal District.
units.label: Growing Risks of Labor Shortages · “Against the backdrop of labor shortages, unemployment measured…”

units.locator: Growing Risks of Labor Shortages
units.text: Risks of labor shortages are unevenly distributed spatially, and prospective employment locations may not coincide with territories where labor is excessively concentrated. Thus, under the Strategy for Socioeconomic Development of the Siberian Federal District up to 2035, 377.6 thousand new jobs will be created in the Siberian Federal District by 2030. Meanwhile, according to the demographic forecast of the Federal State Statistics Service up to 2046, the working-age population in the Siberian Federal District will grow by only 270 thousand by 2030 relative to 2024. This creates a need to attract labor, including from other federal districts of the Russian Federation.
units.label: Growing Risks of Labor Shortages · “Risks of labor shortages are unevenly distributed spatially,…”

units.locator: Increasing Impact of Scientific and Technological Progress on the Spatial Development of the Russian Federation

units.locator: Increasing Impact of Scientific and Technological Progress on the Spatial Development of the Russian Federation
units.text: The spatial development of the Russian Federation is influenced by technological progress, including the sharp acceleration of the creation and dissemination of qualitatively new technologies.

units.locator: Increasing Impact of Scientific and Technological Progress on the Spatial Development of the Russian Federation
units.text: Russian science currently serves as the foundation for the sovereign development of the state, creating the necessary prerequisites and conditions for well-founded, balanced and effective solutions to the full range of social, economic, cultural and other tasks facing the Russian Federation and for ensuring the country’s security. Science makes a significant contribution to humanity’s intellectual heritage. The need to support domestic science has increased particularly since 2022, following the introduction of restrictions against the Russian Federation by unfriendly states. The role of constituent entities of the Russian Federation is increasing at the new stage of technological development. At the same time, the following trends persist:

units.locator: Climate Change
units.text: According to the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change, global greenhouse gas concentrations and air temperatures have been increasing since the 1970s. As of 2020, the global mean near-surface air temperature was 1.1 degrees Celsius above the preindustrial level of 1850–1900.
units.label: Climate Change · “According to the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change,…”

units.locator: Climate Change
units.text: Since the mid-1970s, the annual mean near-surface air temperature in the Russian Federation has been rising by an average of 0.5 degrees Celsius per 10 years, and by 0.7 degrees Celsius per 10 years in the Arctic Zone of the Russian Federation, at a rate 2.8 times the global rate.

units.locator: Climate Change
units.text: Climate change has consequences for human and natural systems and poses risks to security and sustainable development.

units.locator: Climate Change
units.text: Changes are observed in the agroclimatic characteristics of agricultural crops, increases in the frequency and duration of heat, a decline in the load-bearing capacity of permafrost ground, and other changes in climatic characteristics.
units.label: Climate Change · “Changes are observed in the agroclimatic characteristics of…”

units.locator: Climate Change
units.text: Recent decades have seen increases in precipitation, the total annual runoff of Russian rivers, although annual runoff in some major rivers is declining, and associated adverse and hazardous phenomena. According to the Third Assessment Report on Climate Change and Its Consequences in the Russian Federation, more than 142 thousand people underwent evacuation or forced relocation due to natural disasters during 2010–2020.

units.locator: Climate Change
units.text: Depending on climate change scenarios, near-surface air temperature in the Russian Federation may rise by 2–3.3 degrees Celsius by mid-century compared with the beginning of the twenty-first century. Annual precipitation totals are also expected to increase by 8–12 percent. The area occupied by near-surface permafrost may shrink by 15–38 percent.

units.locator: Intensification of the Use of Marine Areas
units.text: Intensification of the Use of Marine Areas
units.label: Intensification of the Use of Marine Areas

units.locator: Intensification of the Use of Marine Areas
units.text: Economic activity in marine areas and coastal territories is unevenly concentrated, leading to conflicts between types of marine use and disturbing the balance between marine use and the condition of marine and coastal ecosystems. The uneven distribution of coastal economic activity is particularly pronounced in the northern and Far Eastern territories of the Russian Federation, where mineral extraction is intensifying under difficult hydrometeorological conditions.
units.label: Intensification of the Use of Marine Areas · “Economic activity in marine areas and coastal territories is…”

units.locator: Intensification of the Use of Marine Areas
units.text: Use of biological resources is also intensifying, as reflected in the development of aquaculture and the transition from coastal fishing to fishing in remote areas of the World Ocean.
units.label: Intensification of the Use of Marine Areas · “Use of biological resources is also intensifying, as reflected…”

units.locator: Intensification of the Use of Marine Areas
units.text: These trends require the introduction of planning mechanisms that synchronize development plans for coastal territories with plans for using adjacent marine space. Most countries sharing a maritime boundary with the Russian Federation, primarily European Union countries, have established marine spatial planning systems that, by imposing restrictions on types of activity within national exclusive economic zones, enable efficient use of marine resources with minimal environmental impact.
units.label: Intensification of the Use of Marine Areas · “These trends require the introduction of planning mechanisms…”

units.locator: III. Analysis of Spatial Development Trends and Plans in Partner Countries and Bordering States of Strategic Importance to the Russian Federation
units.text: III. Analysis of Spatial Development Trends and Plans in Partner Countries and Bordering States of Strategic Importance to the Russian Federation
units.label: III. Analysis of Spatial Development Trends and Plans in Partner Countries and Bordering States of Strategic Importance to the Russian Federation

units.locator: III. Analysis of Spatial Development Trends and Plans in Partner Countries and Bordering States of Strategic Importance to the Russian Federation
units.text: The territory of the Russian Federation shares land borders with 16 states, 7 of which are included in the list of foreign states and territories committing unfriendly acts against the Russian Federation and Russian legal entities and individuals, approved by Executive Order of the Government of the Russian Federation of 5 March 2022 No. 430-р. Most of the other bordering states are important trade and geopolitical partners of the Russian Federation.
units.label: III. Analysis of Spatial Development Trends and Plans in Partner Countries and Bordering States of Strategic Importance to the Russian Federation · “The territory of the Russian Federation shares land borders…”

units.locator: III. Analysis of Spatial Development Trends and Plans in Partner Countries and Bordering States of Strategic Importance to the Russian Federation
units.text: Unlawful unilateral restrictive measures by unfriendly states are resulting in a reorientation of economic ties and accelerated cooperation with other states, including the People’s Republic of China, the Republic of Türkiye, the Republic of India, the Islamic Republic of Iran, Mongolia, countries of the Commonwealth of Independent States other than Ukraine, and states of Southeast Asia, the Middle East, North Africa and Latin America.
units.label: III. Analysis of Spatial Development Trends and Plans in Partner Countries and Bordering States of Strategic Importance to the Russian Federation · “Unlawful unilateral restrictive measures by unfriendly states…”

units.locator: III. Analysis of Spatial Development Trends and Plans in Partner Countries and Bordering States of Strategic Importance to the Russian Federation
units.text: Numerous intergovernmental treaties and agreements are in force, covering virtually all areas of cooperation with those countries.

units.text: The main areas of potential interaction and integration with neighboring states that are not classified as unfriendly include:

units.locator: III. Analysis of Spatial Development Trends and Plans in Partner Countries and Bordering States of Strategic Importance to the Russian Federation
units.text: Since 2010, the People’s Republic of China has been the Russian Federation’s main trading partner. In 2023, bilateral trade between the countries increased by 23.1 percent compared with 2022, exceeding 228 billion US dollars.
units.label: III. Analysis of Spatial Development Trends and Plans in Partner Countries and Bordering States of Strategic Importance to the Russian Federation · “Since 2010, the People’s Republic of China has been the Russian…”

units.locator: III. Analysis of Spatial Development Trends and Plans in Partner Countries and Bordering States of Strategic Importance to the Russian Federation
units.text: In 2023, the physical volume of exports to the Republic of Türkiye increased by 25.2 percent relative to 2021, while exports to the Republic of India increased almost 10-fold.
units.label: III. Analysis of Spatial Development Trends and Plans in Partner Countries and Bordering States of Strategic Importance to the Russian Federation · “In 2023, the physical volume of exports to the Republic of…”

units.locator: III. Analysis of Spatial Development Trends and Plans in Partner Countries and Bordering States of Strategic Importance to the Russian Federation
units.text: A high level of cooperation is maintained with most countries of the Commonwealth of Independent States. The Russian Federation’s largest trade volumes are with the Republic of Belarus, the Republic of Kazakhstan, the Republic of Uzbekistan, the Republic of Armenia, the Republic of Azerbaijan and the Kyrgyz Republic.
units.label: III. Analysis of Spatial Development Trends and Plans in Partner Countries and Bordering States of Strategic Importance to the Russian Federation · “A high level of cooperation is maintained with most countries…”

units.locator: III. Analysis of Spatial Development Trends and Plans in Partner Countries and Bordering States of Strategic Importance to the Russian Federation
units.text: The main plans of friendly states affecting the interests of the Russian Federation concern the implementation of international transport corridor projects and infrastructure projects, as well as the expansion of economic cooperation, primarily through increased bilateral trade.
units.label: III. Analysis of Spatial Development Trends and Plans in Partner Countries and Bordering States of Strategic Importance to the Russian Federation · “The main plans of friendly states affecting the interests of…”

units.locator: III. Analysis of Spatial Development Trends and Plans in Partner Countries and Bordering States of Strategic Importance to the Russian Federation
units.text: The Republic of Azerbaijan and the Islamic Republic of Iran are developing the infrastructure of the North–South International Transport Corridor, which will not only promote growth in the Russian Federation’s trade with those countries but also, in the longer term, create a new alternative trade route with the Republic of India and countries of the Middle East and Southeast Asia. The Republic of Azerbaijan also plans to increase the capacity of checkpoints on the state border with the Russian Federation and develop export infrastructure for transporting oil and gas.
units.label: III. Analysis of Spatial Development Trends and Plans in Partner Countries and Bordering States of Strategic Importance to the Russian Federation · “The Republic of Azerbaijan and the Islamic Republic of Iran are…”

units.locator: III. Analysis of Spatial Development Trends and Plans in Partner Countries and Bordering States of Strategic Importance to the Russian Federation
units.text: The Belt and Road concept promoted by the People’s Republic of China combines the Silk Road Economic Belt and the Twenty-First-Century Maritime Silk Road projects. Implementation of this concept involves creating a network of international routes for rapid delivery of large volumes of Chinese goods abroad and initiating transport, logistics, infrastructure and other projects.
units.label: III. Analysis of Spatial Development Trends and Plans in Partner Countries and Bordering States of Strategic Importance to the Russian Federation · “The Belt and Road concept promoted by the People’s Republic of…”

units.locator: III. Analysis of Spatial Development Trends and Plans in Partner Countries and Bordering States of Strategic Importance to the Russian Federation
units.text: In a trilateral format under the Program for Establishing the China–Mongolia–Russia Economic Corridor, work is under way to implement projects in transport, electricity, customs regulation, industry, environmental protection, science and tourism. The parties have identified as a priority a project to modernize the Russian-Mongolian enterprise Ulaanbaatar Railway Joint Stock Company. The three parties are examining the construction of a gas pipeline from the Russian Federation to the People’s Republic of China through Mongolia.

units.locator: III. Analysis of Spatial Development Trends and Plans in Partner Countries and Bordering States of Strategic Importance to the Russian Federation
units.text: Interregional and intraregional transport routes are being developed in territories along the Russian-Chinese state border.
units.label: III. Analysis of Spatial Development Trends and Plans in Partner Countries and Bordering States of Strategic Importance to the Russian Federation · “Interregional and intraregional transport routes are being…”

units.locator: III. Analysis of Spatial Development Trends and Plans in Partner Countries and Bordering States of Strategic Importance to the Russian Federation
units.text: The Republic of Türkiye and the Republic of India are increasing purchases of Russian energy resources, which will require expansion of Russian logistics infrastructure. Demand for energy resources is also growing in Southeast Asian countries. These factors may affect the utilization of ports in the Azov–Black Sea and Far Eastern basins, respectively, and the routes serving them.
units.label: III. Analysis of Spatial Development Trends and Plans in Partner Countries and Bordering States of Strategic Importance to the Russian Federation · “The Republic of Türkiye and the Republic of India are…”

units.locator: III. Analysis of Spatial Development Trends and Plans in Partner Countries and Bordering States of Strategic Importance to the Russian Federation
units.text: Economic development trends in neighboring states and prospective partner countries may affect the development of individual sectors, including in border territories of the Russian Federation. To ensure economic growth in border territories, priority support must be given to sectors that enable cooperative links with border areas of neighboring friendly countries.
units.label: III. Analysis of Spatial Development Trends and Plans in Partner Countries and Bordering States of Strategic Importance to the Russian Federation · “Economic development trends in neighboring states and…”

units.locator: III. Analysis of Spatial Development Trends and Plans in Partner Countries and Bordering States of Strategic Importance to the Russian Federation
units.text: The Republic of Belarus is the Russian Federation’s main trading partner among the countries of the Commonwealth of Independent States. In 2023, it accounted for 45 percent of the Russian Federation’s trade with countries of the Commonwealth of Independent States. The key area of bilateral cooperation is deepening integration within the Union State, encompassing all spheres of interaction.
units.label: III. Analysis of Spatial Development Trends and Plans in Partner Countries and Bordering States of Strategic Importance to the Russian Federation · “The Republic of Belarus is the Russian Federation’s main…”

units.locator: III. Analysis of Spatial Development Trends and Plans in Partner Countries and Bordering States of Strategic Importance to the Russian Federation
units.text: Comprehensive work is being carried out to implement the Main Directions for Implementing the Provisions of the Treaty on the Establishment of the Union State for 2024–2026, which provide for the development of joint production, protection of technological sovereignty and creation of new industrial capacity to ensure the economic stability of the Union State.
units.label: III. Analysis of Spatial Development Trends and Plans in Partner Countries and Bordering States of Strategic Importance to the Russian Federation · “Comprehensive work is being carried out to implement the Main…”

units.locator: III. Analysis of Spatial Development Trends and Plans in Partner Countries and Bordering States of Strategic Importance to the Russian Federation
units.text: Joint cooperative projects in industry, construction and agriculture are planned in regions of the Russian Federation and the Republic of Belarus.
units.label: III. Analysis of Spatial Development Trends and Plans in Partner Countries and Bordering States of Strategic Importance to the Russian Federation · “Joint cooperative projects in industry, construction and…”

units.locator: III. Analysis of Spatial Development Trends and Plans in Partner Countries and Bordering States of Strategic Importance to the Russian Federation
units.text: In 2023, the border regions of Vitebsk, Gomel and Mogilev Oblasts accounted for 28.5 percent of the country’s gross domestic product. Projects aimed at ensuring technological independence and producing high-value-added products are planned in those regions, including for sale in the markets of Eurasian Economic Union countries.
units.label: III. Analysis of Spatial Development Trends and Plans in Partner Countries and Bordering States of Strategic Importance to the Russian Federation · “In 2023, the border regions of Vitebsk, Gomel and Mogilev…”

units.locator: III. Analysis of Spatial Development Trends and Plans in Partner Countries and Bordering States of Strategic Importance to the Russian Federation
units.text: The oblasts of the Republic of Kazakhstan bordering the Russian Federation account for 35.7 percent of the country’s gross domestic product. The regions differ substantially in economic potential: Atyrau Oblast contributes 12.4 percent, whereas North Kazakhstan Oblast contributes 1.8 percent. Cooperation between the Russian Federation and the Republic of Kazakhstan includes joint projects for the extraction and processing of natural gas and chromium ore and the development of deep grain processing.
units.label: III. Analysis of Spatial Development Trends and Plans in Partner Countries and Bordering States of Strategic Importance to the Russian Federation · “The oblasts of the Republic of Kazakhstan bordering the Russian…”

units.locator: III. Analysis of Spatial Development Trends and Plans in Partner Countries and Bordering States of Strategic Importance to the Russian Federation
units.text: The length of the continuous Russian-Kazakh border, 7.6 thousand kilometers, underpins joint cooperation in developing the North–South International Transport Corridor, including the Belarus–Russia–Kazakhstan–Uzbekistan–Afghanistan–Pakistan route.
units.label: III. Analysis of Spatial Development Trends and Plans in Partner Countries and Bordering States of Strategic Importance to the Russian Federation · “The length of the continuous Russian-Kazakh border, 7.6…”
